text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thurday:
- Swiss parliament plans to address initiatives dealing with the creation of a Holocaust fund during its next session in March.

- Switzerland expects to register a total public-sector budget deficit of 9.4 billion Swiss francs in 1997, one billion more than orignially planned, according to economics magazine 'Die Volkswirtschaft'.
- Alusuisse-Lonza registered an eight percent rise in net profit to 417 million Swiss francs in 1996, sales reached eight billion francs, up from 7.5 billion.

- The Swiss government is expected to decide today on the creation of a special fund to help Holocaust victims immediately. This would mean that the 100 million Swiss francs, that have been paid in by Swiss banks last week, could be handed over to victims very soon.
- Siska, which produces chemical goods for construction, announced that 1996 profits will exceed profit expectations of 50 to 54 million Swiss francs.

- Swiss textile sector had a bad year yet again, as sales dropped to 2.78 billion Swiss francs. However, insiders believe that the weak franc and new tax regulations could lead to an upswing of the textile industry in Switzerland.

- Swiss technoloy group Alusuisse told journalists on Wednesday that the company will also contribute to the 100 million franc Holocaust memorial fund, which was launched by three leading Swiss banks last week.
- Swiss chololate exports in 1996 dropped marginally from 1.168 to 1.152 billion Swiss francs.
